title: AI Assistant for Game Design & Strategy
author: Ok_Shallot4022
selftext:
Hey r/gamedev 👋



I'm building an AI tool specifically for indie game designers — not for coding, but for the creative/strategy side that usually takes hours of solo thinking.



The idea: You type your game concept, and the AI brainstorms with you like a co-designer. It suggests:

• Unique mechanics that fit your genre

• Gameplay loops tailored for your platform (Roblox, mobile, PC indie)

• Monetization strategies ranked by what works for your audience

• Potential weak points in your design before you build



Basically like having a game design partner available 24/7, no experience needed on their end.



Before I spend months building this, I want to ask you guys honestly:



❓ Do you ever feel stuck when brainstorming mechanics or direction for your game?

❓ Would something like this actually save you time — or do you prefer working through design solo?

❓ What would make you actually pay for a tool like this (even $5-15/month)?



No pitch here. I'm just a builder in early validation mode and your honest feedback matters more than 100 YESes from people who don't make games.



Drop your thoughts below — brutal honesty welcome 🙏

comments.author: loopywolf
comments.body: Better than what Claude/ChatGPT/Character.ai and Gemini do already?

replies.author: Ok_Shallot4022
replies.body:
"Hey Loopywolf, thanks for the honest feedback. You're right — ChatGPT can brainstorm mechanics.

But here's what I realized: You're not using ChatGPT to brainstorm once. You're doing it 20+ times, forgetting context, copy-pasting outputs into Google Docs, losing versions.

What if instead of 'another AI tool,' there was a workspace where:

* Your game design evolves across 20 conversations (not lost each time)
* One click exports a full Game Design Document (ready to share with your team)
* You see what mechanics worked for other successful indie games in your genre

Would THAT change your answer? If so, I want to build exactly that instead

replies.author: loopywolf
replies.body:
True, it is better with agents, but there is a way around that

One click does - it outputs an obsidian linked up markdown

replies.author: Ok_Shallot4022
replies.body: That's exactly right. So here's the question: If I spent the next 3 months collecting and analyzing 100+ successful indie game postmortems + interviews with developers who've shipped games — building a database of 'what actually worked. Would that change your answer? Would something like that be worth $15/month to you?

comments.author: KevinDL
comments.body:
First, if you want meaningful feedback here, you should put in the effort to rewrite your post instead of lazily copying and pasting it from r/gamedev.

More importantly, this idea does not solve anything existing AI services cannot already do, mostly for free. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and others can brainstorm mechanics, suggest gameplay loops, discuss monetization, and identify potential weaknesses.

Once brainstorming is finished, developers can move into game development-specific tools like Bezi to build and iterate on the idea directly inside their project.

AI can help you think through a design, but it cannot tell you whether the game is actually fun. Only building, playing, and testing it can do that. Another brainstorming chatbot does not meaningfully close that gap.

replies.author: Ok_Shallot4022
replies.body:
Hey Kevin, thanks for the honest feedback. You're right — most of AI Agents such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini can brainstorm mechanics.   
But here's what I realized: You're not using ChatGPT to brainstorm once. You're doing it 20+ times, forgetting context, copy-pasting outputs into Google Docs, losing versions.

replies.author: KevinDL
replies.body:
That sounds less like a missing product and more like people not understanding how to use the tools they already have.

The game development-specific tool I mentioned, Bezi, already addresses this by letting developers provide persistent project context and evergreen instructions to the LLM. Other major AI services also offer ways to organize projects, retain context, and work with documents.

Is there an education problem around using AI effectively? Absolutely. But you are still not solving a new problem. These solutions already exist if people learn to use AI as more than a disposable prompt box.

replies.author: Ok_Shallot4022
replies.body:
You're right Kevin. I'm not building another tool. I'm building education + a game design knowledge base.   
Question: Would you pay for a course that teaches?   
1/ How to use Claude/AI effectively for game design (step by step)  
2/ Analysis of 100+ successful indie games (what worked, what didn't)Prompts + templates you can use immediately  
3/  A database of game design patterns that shipped

Would that be more valuable than another tool?

replies.author: KevinDL
replies.body:
No, all those resources are already out there for free.  

You seem set on trying to solve a problem that doesn't exist.  And the problem you now want to pivot towards fights against human nature.  

If people want to learn they have everything they need already.
